title: The Scramble for Africa

cards.h: In 1870 about a tenth of Africa was ruled by Europeans. By 1914, almost all of it
cards.b:
Imagine losing control of your continent in about 40 years. That is what happened in Africa. Only Ethiopia and Liberia stayed independent.

How? Guns, medicine, railways and a very unusual conference where no African was invited.
Quinine fought malaria. Steamships went up rivers. The rapid-fire Maxim gun (1884) gave Europeans a huge advantage in battle.

German chancellor Bismarck hosted a conference in Berlin (November 1884-February 1885). Fourteen states attended, none African. They agreed that to claim land, a power needed 'effective occupation'. It did not draw Africa's map by itself; the carve-up was already under way. But it sparked a rush.

King Leopold II of Belgium got recognition of the 'Congo Free State' in 1885 as nearly his personal property. Forced rubber collection brought mutilation and killing. Millions died; estimates vary and are debated, with figures like 10 million often cited. After campaigns by E. D. Morel and others, Belgium took it over in 1908.

Africans resisted all over. At Adwa on 1 March 1896, Emperor Menelik II of Ethiopia crushed an Italian army. The Boer War (1899-1902) pitted Britain against Dutch settlers. In German South West Africa, the Herero and Nama genocide (1904-08) killed tens of thousands.

Borders were often straight lines that split peoples and joined rivals. Many modern African conflicts have roots there.

cards.h: Did Berlin 'divide Africa' in one meeting?
cards.b: Myth: European leaders sat in Berlin and cut up a map.Fact: the conference dealt with the Congo and the rules for claiming land. Most borders were set later through treaties between powers, and many by field agents. Still, no African ruler had a say, and that is the heart of the injustice.

Five things to remember

  1. By 1914 Europe controlled almost all Africa.
  2. The Berlin Conference (1884-85) set the rules, with no Africans present.
  3. Leopold's Congo was among the worst.
  4. Ethiopia won at Adwa (1896).
  5. Indians built the Uganda Railway.

Think about it

  • Why did Europe rush in at that moment?
  • What does Adwa teach?
